facts.fact: MP Sahar Albazar writes that Egypt's draft AI bill bans prohibited AI systems outright, requires prior approval for high-risk ones, and mandates algorithmic fairness, transparency and auditability.

EGY.note: Names no government body using an AI system; only strategy aims and training.

facts.fact: MP Sahar Albazar describes a draft AI law with three risk tiers (prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk) that is still progressing towards final legislation.

EGY.note: Only says AI is being integrated into health, education and infrastructure projects, with no tool or output named.

facts.fact: The document says the president unveiled Egypt's second National AI Strategy (2025-2030) in January 2025, after a first strategy launched in May 2021.

The document says a National AI Council was established under the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology to oversee implementation of the first National AI Strategy launched in May 2021.

EGY.note: Mentions AI research centres in general terms only; no model, dataset or computing named.
Mentions the 2020 Personal Data Protection Law only as a reference point for the AI bill; says nothing on its standing, authority or application.
Lists the urban-rural digital divide as a challenge only; no programme or survey figures.
Names only Egypt Vision 2030 and AI strategies; no national digital strategy described.
Policy dialogues co-hosted with the American University in Cairo are not described as research or publication.

facts.fact: MP Sahar Albazar writes that the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology hosted a listening session on the AI bill for the private sector, attended by over 70 companies and experts who gave recommendations to government officials.
facts.system: MCIT private-sector listening session on the AI bill

EGY.note: Date of the session is not given; publication month used.
Mentions AI incubators as an incentive in the AI bill only; no startup law, label or fund.
Names no hub or park in service.
